one_liner: Senior Treasury policy job writing and implementing strategies against money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions evasion, briefing senior officials and engaging foreign governments.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, people skills, and government-client consulting at IEM are relevant, but the posting requires one year of GS-12 or GS-13 level experience in ALL listed areas, including monitoring AML/CFT developments and creating policies on illicit financial threats. Emergency-management consulting does not obviously cover AML/CFT, so unless Daniel's IEM work touched financial crimes, sanctions, or related national-security finance, Daniel likely will not qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens or nationals) under Direct-Hire authority, so no federal status is needed and rating/ranking and veterans' preference do not apply.

GS-13 requires one year of GS-12-equivalent experience in ALL four areas: monitoring illicit finance/AML/CFT, creating illicit-finance policies or strategies, communicating research and analysis, and engaging the public, international organizations, or foreign governments.
GS-14 requires one year of GS-13-equivalent experience, including independently creating illicit-finance policies and making recommendations to senior decision makers.
The position requires a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance and a background investigation, plus a Confidential Financial Disclosure and ethics/conflict-of-interest review.
All qualifications must be met by the closing date, November 11, 2026.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether any IEM work involved financial crimes, fraud, grant or disaster-fund integrity, sanctions, or national-security finance. If none of it did, a 'not qualified' determination is likely, so treat this as a stretch application.

If IEM work included disaster-recovery fraud prevention, improper-payment controls, or financial-risk analysis for government clients, frame it explicitly as monitoring illicit financial activity and developing mitigation strategies, using the posting's wording.
On the two-page resume, write one tight bullet for each of the four specialized-experience elements. Include month/day/year dates and hours per week for every job.
Answer the questionnaire truthfully and back every 'expert' or 'performed independently' answer with resume text, because unsupported claims lead to disqualification.

Complete the four optional 200-word essays to show mission alignment and your policy, congressional, and stakeholder-engagement strengths. Opt in to sharing your application with other Treasury bureaus.
Apply by November 11, 2026. Also consider better-fit roles, such as FEMA or DHS emergency-management positions, Virginia VDEM, Prince William County emergency management, or congressional staff jobs.
resume_bullets: Monitored [specific financial-risk or fraud trends] for [government client] and produced [number] analytic briefs recommending [policy/strategy actions] to [senior official level] ([dates], [hours]/week).
Drafted [policy papers/briefing materials/reports] on [topic] for [client agency] leadership, coordinating input from [number] federal, state, and local stakeholders.
Engaged [public audiences/officials/partner organizations] on [policy issue] through [meetings/presentations], resulting in [factual outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you developed a policy or strategy to counter a financial or security threat. What was your role, and what happened?
How would you brief a senior Treasury official on a complex AML/CFT development in five minutes?
Tell us about representing your organization to outside stakeholders who disagreed with your position.
How do you stay current on illicit-finance developments such as sanctions evasion or kleptocracy?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requires AML/CFT and illicit-finance policy work in ALL listed areas, which emergency-management consulting likely does not meet.
The position requires SCI clearance eligibility, financial disclosure, and ethics review, which add time and scrutiny.
This is a senior GS-13/14 position with no lower-grade entry, so a lack of directly comparable experience will screen you out.
